recent_posts.title: Introducing Chunk sidecars: Inner loop validation that keeps up with your agents
recent_posts.summary: CircleCI introduces Chunk sidecars, lightweight microVM environments that run alongside AI coding agents during local development to validate changes before they reach CI. As AI agents flood CI pipelines with unreviewed commits, sidecars restore balance by running scoped 'microbuilds' within 60 seconds, catching failures locally while the agent is still in context. The tool is agent-agnostic (works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, etc.), auto-detects your tech stack, supports environment snapshots for team sharing, and ensures parity with CI environments. Available now in preview for paid CircleCI plan customers.

recent_posts.title: Shipping trustworthy code with Chunk CLI
recent_posts.summary: Chunk CLI is a tool that bridges the gap between AI coding agents and team-specific code quality standards. It works in three stages: `build-prompt` mines real GitHub PR review history to generate a team-specific review prompt; `chunk init` and `chunk skill install` wire commit gates and review skills into Claude Code via lifecycle hooks so tests and linting run automatically before every commit; and `chunk task` hands off systematic fixes to autonomous CircleCI pipeline agents that validate changes and open PRs. The tutorial walks through each command against a sample TypeScript/Node.js API project, showing how recurring review patterns (security, input validation, TypeScript safety) get encoded, enforced locally, and applied at scale in CI.

recent_posts.title: Terminal dependencies for CircleCI workflows: Always run what matters
recent_posts.summary: CircleCI has introduced terminal job dependencies, allowing teams to define jobs that run after upstream work finishes regardless of whether those jobs succeeded, failed, or were canceled. Using the `terminal` state in `requires`, you can express 'run this when upstream work is done, no matter how it ended' without duplicating config or adding fragile conditional branches. Common use cases include always tearing down ephemeral environments after tests and sending a single final notification without creating separate jobs for each outcome. The feature reduces repetitive config, clarifies workflow intent, and lowers operational risk from missed cleanup paths.

recent_posts.title: How to set up rolling deployments with CircleCI
recent_posts.summary: A step-by-step guide to setting up rolling deployments on Kubernetes using CircleCI. Covers writing Kubernetes manifests with maxSurge and maxUnavailable for zero-downtime deploys, building and pushing Docker images via CircleCI pipelines, adding deploy markers for visibility in the Deploys dashboard, monitoring rollouts with kubectl, troubleshooting common issues like stuck rollouts and CrashLoopBackOff, and setting up an automated rollback pipeline triggered from the CircleCI dashboard. Also discusses when rolling deployments are appropriate versus blue-green or canary strategies.

recent_posts.title: CircleCI is now available as a Codex plugin
recent_posts.summary: CircleCI has launched a plugin for OpenAI's Codex, enabling developers to manage CI/CD pipelines directly within the Codex agent. The plugin supports pipeline monitoring, build debugging, config optimization, CLI operations, and autonomous CI/CD maintenance via CircleCI's Chunk agent. Users can invoke it with simple prompts like '@circleci diagnose the latest failing build' without leaving their local environment.

recent_posts.title: Building an agentic content production system with Claude Code
recent_posts.summary: A content marketing director at CircleCI shares how their five-person team adapted Claude Code's .claude folder structure to build a full content production system called the Content Workflow Manager. The system encodes institutional knowledge — voice guidelines, a four-stage review process with distinct AI personas (Corrector, Webcrawler, Censor, Focus Group), team routing logic, and six invocable skill workflows — into files Claude reads before every session. Skills cover the full lifecycle from SEO post drafting through Contentful publish prep and social distribution, plus an issue management layer called THE GUILD that integrates with Linear for sprint planning, triage, and weekly leadership summaries. The post is candid about maturity: the review workflow and issue management are solid, the tutorial lane is still being tuned, and the system has already expanded beyond blog posts to general team operations.

recent_posts.title: Cirrus CI is shutting down: upgrade to a scalable, AI-ready alternative
recent_posts.summary: Cirrus Labs announced they are joining OpenAI, resulting in Cirrus CI shutting down on June 1, 2026. CircleCI positions itself as a migration target, mapping Cirrus CI concepts (tasks→jobs, container→docker executor, etc.) to CircleCI equivalents. Key advantages highlighted include native GitHub/GitLab/Bitbucket support, Apple M4 Pro macOS runners, intelligent test splitting, dynamic configuration, an Orbs ecosystem, and AI-native tooling including an MCP Server and an autonomous CI/CD agent called Chunk. The post includes a migration concept mapping table and details on free tiers for open source projects.

recent_posts.title: 7 lessons for driving AI tool adoption across engineering teams
recent_posts.summary: Superhuman's CTO Loïc Houssier shares seven practical lessons for driving AI tool adoption across engineering teams. Key strategies include removing procurement friction so engineers can self-serve tool licenses, forming an AI guild for peer knowledge sharing, recruiting respected skeptics rather than enthusiasts to build credibility, scheduling quarterly retooling time, starting hesitant engineers on low-stakes non-code tasks, running separate SDLCs for different product risk levels, and investing in evals to manage shared quality ownership in prompt-driven features.

recent_posts.title: Deployment strategies: Types, trade-offs, and how to choose
recent_posts.summary: A comprehensive overview of software deployment strategies covering big bang, rolling, blue-green, canary, A/B testing, shadow, feature flag, immutable, and GitOps-based deployments. Each strategy is explained with how it works, its trade-offs between risk and complexity, and when to use it. The guide also covers how to choose the right strategy based on five factors: downtime tolerance, infrastructure budget, team maturity, architecture type, and compliance requirements. Practical CI/CD pipeline integration examples using CircleCI, Argo Rollouts, and ArgoCD are included, along with best practices like automating rollback, separating deploy from release, and handling database migrations with the expand-migrate-contract pattern.

recent_posts.title: What are test hooks in AI-native development?
recent_posts.summary: Test hooks connect test and lint commands to lifecycle events in AI coding agents like Claude Code and Cursor. When an event fires (e.g., after a file edit or at session end), the registered command runs automatically and blocks the agent's action if it fails. This creates deterministic local validation that doesn't rely on prompts or agent memory. The post explains the three components of a test hook (event, command, blocking behavior), best practices for layering checks across the agent lifecycle, how hooks complement CI/CD rather than replace it, and how CircleCI's open-source Chunk CLI scaffolds the full setup including an AI code review layer driven by your team's actual PR history.
